ety.text: Literally, “What is not done is all towards the best”. Paraphrase of a passage from G.W. Leibniz's Theodicy in 1710: "God, although He always chooses the best, does not act out of absolute necessity, that the laws prescribed by God to nature, based on conformity, occupy a middle position between geometrical truths, absolutely necessary, and arbitrary decisions". Later satirised by Voltaire to mock naive optimism.
